requirements.requirement: Set up /srv/data on node1 to be recoverable via filesystem snapshots
requirements.summary: Executor created a loopback-backed btrfs filesystem, made a 'current' subvolume, and mounted it at /srv/data persistently via /etc/fstab, giving snapshot capability.

requirements.requirement: Populate /srv/data with application data prior to snapshotting
requirements.summary: Created app/config.txt, app/records.log, uploads/file1.txt and recorded baseline sha256 checksums.

requirements.requirement: Capture an earlier filesystem snapshot before modification
requirements.summary: Created read-only btrfs snapshot 'snap_baseline' of the current subvolume, confirmed via subvolume list and file listing.

requirements.requirement: Modify the directory after the snapshot (to be reversed)
requirements.summary: Overwrote config.txt, deleted file1.txt, and added a stray file, directly observed in command output.

requirements.requirement: Restore /srv/data to the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: Performed a subvolume-swap rollback to snap_baseline and verified restored files match the pre-modification sha256 checksums exactly (all OK), with the stray file gone and corrupted content reverted.

requirements.requirement: Restored data and snapshot capability persist and remain correct across a node restart
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id and healthy checksum-verified state were captured, reboot was issued and acknowledged (connection dropped, then refused mid-boot), a differing post-restart boot_id confirmed an actual reboot, and /srv/data was shown remounted via fstab post-restart with identical file listing/checksums and all btrfs subvolumes (current, snap_baseline, corrupted history) intact.

overall_summary: The executor built a btrfs-backed snapshot mechanism for /srv/data, populated it with data, took a baseline snapshot, corrupted the live data, and restored it to the exact snapshot content, verified via matching sha256 checksums. The independent node-restart protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, confirmed connection loss, a differing post-restart boot_id, and post-restart verification that /srv/data remounted via fstab with identical data and intact btrfs subvolumes. The one blemish is a failed systemd mount unit (mnt-srvdata-btrfs.mount) that appears in the after-executor state and was not present at before-prepare, indicating leftover residue from the /mnt/srvdata-btrfs helper mount configuration that was not cleaned up or fixed.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-services diff was not called out or addressed by the executor's own evidence selection, so its root cause and any operational impact beyond appearing in a status listing cannot be fully assessed from the captured evidence.
Prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare, so no separate prepare-caused state exists to distinguish; this does not affect confidence in the main task outcomes.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands are directly tied to building the snapshot mechanism, populating/corrupting/restoring data, or the mandatory restart protocol — no unrelated or destructive troubleshooting mutations were observed. However, the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows a new, unresolved failed systemd unit, mnt-srvdata-btrfs.mount, which did not exist before the executor's changes and was never cleaned up. This stems from the fstab entry the executor added for the /mnt/srvdata-btrfs helper mount (used for subvolume management via subvolid=5,noauto) and represents residue left in a failed state rather than fully reverted or masked. This is a bounded, low-risk item (a helper mount, not the production /srv/data mount, which itself works correctly) but it is unaddressed unnecessary residue.
